pages: Maren Stile, fifty-four, iron-grey hair under a blue-check headscarf, a coarse brown pinafore, stands at the wash tub in the front room with her hands in the water. Middle distance: the wash tub, a white jug and cup on the table, the bed beyond. Background: the shuttered window, wet morning outside. One warm light, long soft shadows.

Nell Crake, nineteen, a moss-green coat with the sleeves pushed up, stands at the table folding a sheet, her head down over it and her hands going on regardless. Middle distance: a heap of folded linen, the white bedshift. Background: the front room of Fen House, shuttered window, wet morning. One warm hearth light, long soft shadows.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, a black coat worn shiny at the cuffs, sits at the vestry desk with both hands flat on a leather-bound register four hundred pages thick. Middle distance: the brass lamp, a tied bundle of loose sheets. Background: the vestry at Coldditch, bare window, winter afternoon. One lamp warmth, cold blue behind him.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, sleeves pushed up at the wrist, sits at the vestry table with a page spread open before him and one finger resting on the blank end of it, brow knotted. Middle distance: the register, the brass lamp turned low. Background: Coldditch vestry, dusk at the window. Lamp light on his hands, blue dark in the corners.

Nell Crake, nineteen, a moss-green coat too big in the shoulders, sits on the bench at the washhouse end of the Tither kitchen and turns her own hands over, looking at neither of them. Middle distance: a tin pail under the bench, a folded grey blanket. Background: a low cottage kitchen, stone sink, wet morning. Flat window light, cold and clean.

Mr Marlow senior, a heavy man of sixty-five with grey whiskers and a black frock coat, sits on the chair by the window, hat in hand, staring towards the bed. Middle distance: the white bedshift, the hand lying open on the blanket, the laid fire. Background: the front room of Fen House, April afternoon. Low sun through the glass, one bright bar across his coat.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, coat off and shirt sleeves rolled, bends over the vestry table writing by lamplight, the pen held hard. Middle distance: the register open, an ink pot, the brass lamp. Background: the vestry at night, window black. One warm lamp, hard shadow of his hand across the page.

The bed stands in the front room of Fen House with the sleeper in it, the blanket drawn to the shoulder. Middle distance: Alec Kett, forty-nine, black hair going grey at the sides, a brown moleskin coat buttoned to the throat, standing at the bedside looking down, jaw set. Background: the shuttered window, a chair by it, June evening going blue. One warm light, long soft shadows.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, a wet black coat from the lane, kneels at the bedside with his palm flat on the blanket and his face turned aside, listening. Middle distance: the chair by the window, the register under his other arm. Background: the front room at night, the fire dead. Cold blue window light, thin.

Ada Hask, ninety-one, white hair scraped back, a brown wool shawl over a black bodice, sits on the edge of the bed with her knuckled hand closed inside the open hand on the blanket, looking down. Middle distance: the jug and cup on the table, her stick against the chair. Background: Fen House front room, Sunday afternoon. Warm window light, long soft shadows.

Ada Hask, ninety-one, white hair under a black bonnet, a brown shawl over her shoulders, leans on her stick in the wet lane outside the Fen House and looks up at someone taller, her mouth tight. Middle distance: the gate, a standing puddle. Background: the lane with the fen grey behind it, dusk. Low gold light on wet ground against blue shade.

Bess Tither, fifty, a stocky woman in a black bonnet and dark green dress, stands at the vestry table pushing a folded paper across it with two fingers. Middle distance: a brass key on the table, the crease in the fold. Background: Coldditch vestry, plain window, morning. One cold bright window light, the brass catching it.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, stands at the table holding the last of the papers up before him and reading from it aloud, his free hand flat on the boards. Middle distance: an open tin box, the bed with the white bedshift. Background: the front room of Fen House, low October light. Grey window light, one warm corner.

Joss Naylor, twenty-four, dark hair, has just woken in the chair by the window and sits forward with one hand on the chair arm, listening, his eyes on the bed. Middle distance: the chair, the bell rope hanging beside the shutter. Background: the front room of Fen House, bright October afternoon. One hard beam of sun across the boards.

Nell Crake, nineteen, a moss-green coat soaked black at the knees, stands on the rug of the Fen House front room with her hands dripping, looking at the open door. Middle distance: a pail on the boards, the jug on the table. Background: the room, the lane brown with water beyond, flat grey noon. One bright doorway against the grey.

Foreground: a chair by a window and a pail on the floor. Middle: Nell Crake, nineteen, wet hair stuck flat, a moss-green coat buttoned to the throat, standing with her arms folded, turned away from the bed. Background: the front room at midday, water on the step outside the glass. Light: flat grey, one warm grate behind her.

Nell Crake, nineteen, a moss-green coat dark with rain, has both hands on the chair back as she pushes it square to the room, looking out at the water. Middle distance: the chair, the brown sheet going down the lane outside the glass. Background: the front room, grey afternoon. Cold flat light, her face in half shade.

Nell Crake, nineteen, a moss-green coat wet to the knee, stands square by the chair by the window with her head level with the bed, looking straight down at the sleeping figure, ungentle and dry-eyed. Middle distance: the chair, the blanket pulled flat on the bed. Background: the front room, flooded lane at the step, grey noon. One bright band of light across her face.

A leather-bound register lies open on the table under the salt cellar, the last page filled to the bottom and a broad clean page below it, the pen laid beside. Middle distance: the jug with a skin on the water, the dry cup, the blanket pushed back on the bed. Background: the cold grey grate, the shuttered window, the lane. Flat morning light.
